sources.note: Bibliographic check only: the complete Glottolog bibliography tagged [dol] is Shaw 1981 (ms wordlist), Shaw 1986 (overview/wordlist) and Ethnologue; no grammar, grammar sketch, phonology or dictionary exists for Doso or for Turumsa (Turumsa Glottolog's most extensive descriptions are also a wordlist or less).

sources.citation: Greenhill, Simon. TransNewGuinea.org entry 'Doso' (73 lexical items, all from Shaw 1986)
sources.note: Lexical database only; sole source Shaw 1986; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Shaw, R. Daniel. 1986. The Bosavi language family. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 24, 45-76. Pacific Linguistics A-70. Canberra: Research School of Pacific and Asian Studies, ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-A70.45
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The 'cursory phonological examination' (pp.47-49, Table 1) covers /p/~/f/ distribution, consonant and vowel inventories, and supra-segmentals limited to nasalisation, length, labialisation and open/closed syllables for the surveyed Bosavi-family languages; Doso is NOT in Table 1. Doso appears only in note 4 ('no complete wordlists are available') and as a partial wordlist in Appendix A, taken at Kisigi from a Kamula man married to a Doso woman. No stress/accent statement for any language, and none for Doso.

sources.note: Anthropological thesis on the neighbouring Kamula that Shaw cites for the existence and migration of the Doso; very unlikely to contain phonology but is the only other work Shaw names in connection with Doso.

sources.citation: Shaw, Daniel. 1981. Doso. Unpublished ms., 9 pp. (SIL-PNG survey wordlist; Glottolog ref 718134, file held by Glottolog editors, not shareable)

sources.note: The only Doso-specific document known to exist; a survey wordlist may carry phonetic stress marks or a one-line note on accent, though as a 9-page wordlist it probably has no prose phonology.
